title: Sharp Lipschitz Envelope Inference for Singular Modified Treatment Policies
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the sound package subfield below the field floor: it proves matched rates for two engineered planar subclasses, not a general multivariate active-anchor rate theory.
gap_reasons: It does not establish a general rate theory for multivariate policies or characterize rates by active-anchor geometry; the equal-projection identity concerns paired laws, while the minimax extrema are taken over two different, tightly constructed subclasses.

The description of the circle smoothness threshold as ‘necessary and sufficient’ overstates the result: the proof establishes necessity only for making this particular pilot’s squared anchor-learning error negligible, and supplies no minimax impossibility theorem below the threshold.

The load-bearing aggregate-weight argument also compresses the uniform pilot reconstruction and between-mesh C2 control into an underspecified finite-chart step, limiting reproducibility of the feasible estimator proof.

The narrow constructed scope, absence of a substantive policy application, and this technical specification gap keep the projected leading-journal score below the strongest matched-minimax papers despite the field-level theorem.

The headline says the paired common-base-law interventions themselves have different full-endpoint risk/outward-excess rates, but the delivered minimax rates are separate suprema over the ray and circle classes; revise the statement to make the paired projection/margin fact and the separate class-level rate claims explicit, as its proof and thm:equal-projection-rate-separation-above-elbow already do.
proof_attempt_summary: The derivation completed a sound planar-disk construction: paired ray/circle policies have the same projection law and optimizer margin, while their separate policy classes have matched endpoint-risk and honest outward-excess rates; it also supplied tie-valid containment and smoothness nonadaptation. The math referee passed and the Chen--Gao source claims were verified against arXiv v3, but the cold tier referee capped the package at subfield because the results remain two engineered subclasses rather than a general multivariate active-anchor theory. A field-level re-raise must add that general characterization or a substantive application, tighten the finite-chart estimator argument, and separate paired-law wording from class-level minimax suprema.
tldr: Two singular planar modified treatment policies can have the same conditional exterior metric-projection law and the same quadratic optimizer margin but different sharp-envelope inference rates. The concentrated ray class has matched endpoint-risk and honest outward-excess rate \(n^{-\beta/(2\beta+2+\kappa)}\) for every \(\beta>2\). The diffuse-circle class has matched rate \(n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1+\kappa)}\) for \(\beta>\beta_\star(\kappa):=(4-\kappa+\sqrt{\kappa^2+8\kappa+32})/4\), and the equal-projection comparison is made on this common range. The common positive-mass identity contribution is root-\(n\), the deterministic sample-split interval remains jointly honest at ties, and the \(\beta=3\) aggregate-weight calculation discharges the original early-kill gate under merely measurable envelope densities.
gap: Population sharpness of the all-anchor Lipschitz interval is known, but inference in the closest causal work targets a wider interior-displaced one-anchor interval and excludes collapsing policies. Generic codimension rates are also known, but they do not determine whether equal projection laws conceal different optimizer-induced information geometry under vanishing boundary density.
fill: First certify the total clamped policy construction, its common exterior projection law, its root-n inside identity piece, and its concentrated-versus-diffuse exterior active laws; then prove or refute the beta-three aggregate-weight lemma including pilot derivatives, conditional Gram bounds, exterior learned-anchor occupancy, and exceptional moments. If it survives, establish tie-valid joint honesty for the deterministic measurable interval, matched full-endpoint and outward-excess rates, and smoothness nonadaptation on infinite-dimensional nonradial classes.
